sections.h2: Selling a West Seneca house: the basics
sections.html: West Seneca is a built-out Buffalo suburb, so the condition of the house and its paperwork set the timeline more than land does. Central Erie County is home to the town, bordered by Buffalo and Lackawanna on the west, Cheektowaga on the north, Orchard Park on the south, and Elma and Lancaster on the east. It spans 21.4 square miles and has held steady near 45,000 residents since 2000, with 45,500 counted in 2020.

Gardenville and New Ebenezer lie in the north, East Seneca follows Route 16, and Ebenezer is in the center. Cazenovia Creek and Buffalo Creek cross the town.

Roads matter to buyers here. The New York State Thruway (I-90) crosses the western part of town and meets NY 400, the Aurora Expressway, and U.S. 219 reaches the southwest corner. NY 16 (Seneca Street and Center Road) and NY 354 (Clinton Street) run east and west, while NY 240, NY 277 (Union Road) and Transit Road (NY 78) run north and south.

  • Northern streets near Gardenville: close to Cheektowaga and Buffalo.
  • Central Ebenezer and Union Road: near Town Hall.
  • Along Route 16 and NY 400: quick access to the expressway.
  • Southern streets near Orchard Park: edges of the Orchard Park school district.

Public schools come from three districts. West Seneca Central is the largest and serves most addresses, while some parcels fall in Orchard Park Central or the Cheektowaga-Sloan Union Free School District. Find out which one applies before advertising, as it also determines the separate school tax bill. Buyers who ask about schools will expect a straight answer, and having one ready makes the listing look careful.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a West Seneca sale
sections.html:
On top of the state charge, Erie County levies its own transfer tax. Together they come to $4.50 per $500 of price: $2.00 to the state and $2.50 to the county. Prices are rounded up to the next $500. The seller owes it, and it is paid at the clerk's counter when the deed is submitted.

Sellers aged 62 or older who have owned and lived in a single-family or two-family house for at least a year can claim the lower $2.00 rate with an affidavit filed at the clerk's office. Separately, the buyer owes a 1 percent mansion tax once a residential price reaches $1 million.

The clerk's list is brief. Accepted payment includes cash, check, money order, cashier's check, Visa, MasterCard and Discover.

Assessments are handled in Room 211 of Town Hall at 1250 Union Road, and the Town Clerk collects taxes as Receiver from Room 212 down the hall. Town and county bills arrive in mid-January with a February 15 due date, after which a penalty applies. School bills arrive in mid-September with an October 15 due date. The town hands unpaid town and county taxes to Erie County on July 1 and unpaid school taxes on December 1.

Partial payments are accepted in the office. Credit card payments carry a convenience fee of 2.45 percent, and e-checks carry a $1.75 fee. The town discourages bank bill pay because those mailings lack a U.S. postmark. Check the current bill, since due dates and fees are set each year.

Exemption applications for the 2027 roll are due by March 1, 2027. The exemptions on offer include:

  • Senior citizens: a cut of 5 to 50 percent in assessment for homeowners aged 65 and up whose combined income is under $37,400.
  • Persons with disabilities and limited income: the same 5 to 50 percent range, with income under $32,400.
  • Military service: 15 percent of assessed value up to $18,000, with added amounts for combat service and disability.

The state now runs the STAR program directly, and the town no longer accepts STAR applications.

sections.h2: Permits and rental registration before closing
sections.html:
Building, plumbing and electrical permits and their inspections come from the Code Enforcement Office. An inspection is not scheduled without a house number and a permit, and a certificate of code compliance follows only once the required inspections pass. A deck, finished basement or addition built without paperwork is something to raise with the office now, asking how to close it out.

A landlord must also register each rental with the Town Clerk's Office by filing a Rental Housing Business License Application. If the house has had tenants, make sure that registration is current and tell the buyer. The Code Enforcement Office can answer questions at 716-558-3242.

sections.h2: What happens between offer and closing
sections.html:
Several offices handle pieces of a West Seneca sale. Town Hall at 1250 Union Road holds the assessment in Room 211 and the tax collection in Room 212. The Code Enforcement Office has the permit file. The Erie County Clerk records the deed and collects the transfer tax at the counter.

Start by checking the current tax bill. Town and county taxes are due February 15 and school taxes October 15, so the timing of your closing decides who owes which installment. Any balance the town hands to Erie County on July 1 or December 1 has to be cleared with the county before title can move. Ask your attorney to confirm the figures in writing, and remember that the buyer's attorney will ask for the same numbers.

Cash makes sense for a house with open permits, a rental history or deferred repairs, because there is no appraisal to fail. Compare offers by the amount you keep after transfer tax, payoff and tax adjustments.

Ahead of the first showing, gather the deed, current tax bills, permit records and any rental registration. Request a payoff letter from your lender and confirm that everyone on title will sign. Fewer loose ends for the buyer and the title company means a faster close.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax does a West Seneca seller owe?
faqs.a: It is $4.50 per $500 of the price, made up of $2.00 for New York State and $2.50 for Erie County. The seller pays at recording, and the price is rounded up to the next $500.

faqs.q: Do West Seneca seniors get a lower transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: Yes. A seller aged 62 or older who owned and lived in a single-family or two-family house for at least a year can pay $2.00 per $500 instead of $4.50. The Erie County Clerk provides the affidavit at no charge.

faqs.q: Which dates matter on a West Seneca tax bill?
faqs.a: February 15 for town and county taxes, with bills mailed in mid-January, and October 15 for school taxes. Town and county balances move to Erie County on July 1, and school balances move on December 1.

faqs.q: Must a rental house be registered with the town before it is sold?
faqs.a: The town requires rental property owners to register with the Town Clerk's Office through a Rental Housing Business License Application. If the house has been rented, confirm the registration is current before you sell.

faqs.q: Where do West Seneca owners apply for tax exemptions?
faqs.a: At the Assessor's Office, 1250 Union Road, Room 211. Applications for the 2027 roll are due March 1, 2027, and STAR is now run by the state, so contact the New York State Tax Department for that program.
